claim: Hematopoietic stem and progenitor cells (HSPCs) give rise to all blood cell types throughout the life of an organism (Orkin and Zon, 2008).
source: Hematopoietic stem and progenitor cells (HSPCs) give rise to all blood cell types throughout the life of an organism (Orkin and Zon, 2008).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Orkin and Zon, 2008, which is established scientific knowledge in the field.

claim: HSPCs reside in a complex microenvironment called the niche that is made up of many different kinds of support cells, including various types of mesenchymal stromal cells (MSCs) and endothelial cells (ECs) (Pinho and Frenette, 2019).
source: HSPCs reside in a complex microenvironment called the niche that is made up of many different kinds of support cells, including various types of mesenchymal stromal cells (MSCs) and endothelial cells (ECs) (Pinho and Frenette, 2019).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Pinho and Frenette, 2019, representing established knowledge about the HSPC niche composition.

claim: Recently developed transgenic reporter lines have allowed identification of well-defined endogenous HSPCs in both mouse and zebrafish model organisms (Acar et al., 2015; Chen et al., 2016; Christodoulou et al., 2020; Tamplin et al., 2015).
source: Recently developed transgenic reporter lines have allowed identification of well-defined endogenous HSPCs in both mouse and zebrafish model organisms (Acar et al., 2015; Chen et al., 2016; Christodoulou et al., 2020; Tamplin et al., 2015).
evidence: This claim is supported by multiple citations documenting the development of transgenic reporter lines for HSPC identification.

claim: The dynamic behavior of HSPCs in the niche of mouse and zebrafish can be observed using live imaging (Bixel et al., 2017; Christodoulou et al., 2020; Itkin et al., 2016; Koechlein et al., 2016; Lo Celso et al., 2009; Spencer et al., 2014; Tamplin et al., 2015).
source: The dynamic behavior of HSPCs in the niche of mouse and zebrafish can be observed using live imaging (Bixel et al., 2017; Christodoulou et al., 2020; Itkin et al., 2016; Koechlein et al., 2016; Lo Celso et al., 2009; Spencer et al., 2014; Tamplin et al., 2015).
evidence: This claim is supported by multiple citations documenting live imaging studies of HSPCs in their niche.

claim: Certain events during hematopoietic ontogeny, such as the colonization of the fetal bone marrow, have so far only been studied in fixed tissues because they are difficult to access (Coşkun et al., 2014).
source: Certain events during hematopoietic ontogeny, such as the colonization of the fetal bone marrow, have so far only been studied in fixed tissues because they are difficult to access (Coşkun et al., 2014).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Coşkun et al., 2014, indicating a limitation in the field.

claim: Single endogenous HSPCs can be tracked by light microscopy, then identified by serial block-face scanning electron microscopy (SBEM) at multiscale levels.
source: Here, we show that single endogenous HSPCs can be tracked by light microscopy, then identified by serial block-face scanning electron microscopy (SBEM) at multiscale levels.
evidence: This is a primary finding of the study, supported by the experimental data and methods described throughout the manuscript.

claim: Using the zebrafish larval kidney marrow (KM) niche as a model, single fluorescently labeled HSPCs were followed by light sheet microscopy, then their exact location was confirmed in a 3D SBEM dataset.
source: Using the zebrafish larval kidney marrow (KM) niche as a model, we followed single fluorescently labeled HSPCs by light sheet microscopy, then confirmed their exact location in a 3D SBEM dataset.
evidence: This is a primary methodological finding of the study, supported by the experimental workflow described in the manuscript.

claim: A variety of different configurations of HSPCs and surrounding niche cells were found, suggesting there could be functional heterogeneity in sites of HSPC lodgement.
source: We found a variety of different configurations of HSPCs and surrounding niche cells, suggesting there could be functional heterogeneity in sites of HSPC lodgement.
evidence: This claim is based on observations from the SBEM data and is presented as a speculative interpretation of the structural heterogeneity observed.

claim: Dopamine beta-hydroxylase (dbh) positive ganglion cells were identified as a previously uncharacterized functional cell type in the HSPC niche.
source: Our approach also allowed us to identify dopamine beta-hydroxylase (dbh) positive ganglion cells as a previously uncharacterized functional cell type in the HSPC niche.
evidence: This is a primary finding of the study, supported by CLEM data and functional experiments with 6-OHDA.

claim: Bilateral clusters of approximately 50 HSPCs, for a total of approximately 100 HSPCs, were observed in the region of the anterior KM at 5 dpf.
source: We observed bilateral clusters of ~50 HSPCs, for a total of ~100 HSPCs, in the region of the anterior KM at 5 dpf (Figure 1—figure supplement 1A-D).
evidence: This claim is supported by quantification data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1A-D.

claim: During early HSPC colonization of the KM at 4 dpf, approximately 50 total HSPCs were observed, which increased by approximately 100% from 4 to 5–6 dpf, and then again by approximately 50% from 5–6 to 7–8 dpf.
source: During early HSPC colonization of the KM at 4 dpf we observed ~50 total HSPCs, which increased by ~100% from 4 to 5–6 dpf, and then again by ~50% from 5–6 to 7–8 dpf (Figure 1—figure supplement 1E).
evidence: This claim is supported by quantification data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1E.

claim: On average, only one to two mitotic HSPCs were found in the KM at 5 dpf.
source: On average, we only found one to two mitotic HSPCs in the KM at 5 dpf (Figure 1—figure supplement 1F-J).
evidence: This claim is supported by phospho-histone H3 (PH3) antibody labeling data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1F-J.

claim: Previous studies of hematopoietic cells in the larval KM at 7 dpf also showed low levels of proliferation (van Rooijen et al., 2009).
source: Previous studies of hematopoietic cells in the larval KM at 7 dpf also showed low levels of proliferation (van Rooijen et al., 2009).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to van Rooijen et al., 2009.

claim: The increase in HSPC numbers during the early stages of KM colonization results from arrival via circulation, that is HSPCs that originated in the caudal hematopoietic tissue (CHT) and dorsal aorta (Murayama et al., 2006), and not extensive proliferation of resident HSPCs.
source: These data suggest that the increase in HSPC numbers during the early stages of KM colonization results from arrival via circulation, that is HSPCs that originated in the caudal hematopoietic tissue (CHT) and dorsal aorta (Murayama et al., 2006), and not extensive proliferation of resident HSPCs.
evidence: This claim is based on inference from the low proliferation data and is supported by a citation to Murayama et al., 2006 regarding HSPC origins.

claim: Light sheet fluorescence microscopy (Huisken and Stainier, 2009) was used to rapidly capture HSPC colonization events throughout the entire depth of the larval KM.
source: To rapidly capture HSPC colonization events throughout the entire depth of the larval KM, we performed light sheet fluorescence microscopy (Huisken and Stainier, 2009).
evidence: This is a methodological claim supported by citation to the light sheet microscopy technique.

claim: Using light sheet microscopy, a Z stack through the entire KM could be rapidly acquired in less than 30 s (>200 slices with 1 μm spacing).
source: Using this technique, we could rapidly acquire a Z stack through the entire KM in less than 30 s (>200 slices with 1 μm spacing).
evidence: This is a methodological claim describing the imaging parameters used in the study.

claim: Runx:mCherry+ HSPCs were localized within the anterior kidney region, mediolateral to the proximal pronephric tubules.
source: Together with the cdh17:GFP reporter line for pronephric tubules (Zhou et al., 2010), we localized Runx:mCherry+ HSPCs within the anterior kidney region, mediolateral to the proximal pronephric tubules (Figure 1—figure supplement 3).
evidence: This claim is supported by imaging data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 3 and citation to Zhou et al., 2010 for the cdh17:GFP reporter line.

claim: HSPC clusters were located between lateral dorsal aortae and cardinal veins.
source: HSPC clusters were located between lateral dorsal aortae and cardinal veins (Figure 1—figure supplement 4).
evidence: This claim is supported by imaging data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 4.

claim: Rare circulating Runx:GFP+ HSPCs were seen interacting with and lodging in the perivascular niche upon arrival within the anterior kidney region.
source: Upon arrival within the anterior kidney region, rare circulating Runx:GFP+ HSPCs were seen interacting with and lodging in the perivascular niche (Figure 1A).
evidence: This claim is supported by live imaging data shown in Figure 1A.

claim: Single lodged HSPCs were resolved surrounded by ECs in a pocket-like structure, as observed previously in the zebrafish CHT and mouse fetal liver (Tamplin et al., 2015).
source: We resolved single lodged HSPCs surrounded by ECs in a pocket-like structure, as we observed previously in the zebrafish CHT and mouse fetal liver (Tamplin et al., 2015; Figure 1B).
evidence: This claim is supported by imaging data shown in Figure 1B and citation to Tamplin et al., 2015.

claim: Runx:mCherry is a more restricted marker of HSPCs and is expressed in the cytoplasm, allowing cellular morphology to be resolved, while Runx:GFP more broadly labels the progenitor pool and is only localized to the nucleus.
source: As previously described, Runx:GFP is a more restricted marker of HSPCs and is expressed in the cytoplasm, allowing cellular morphology to be resolved, while Runx:mCherry more broadly labels the progenitor pool and is only localized to the nucleus, making it more appropriate for quantifying single cells (Tamplin et al., 2015; Figure 1—figure supplement 5A).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to Tamplin et al., 2015 and imaging data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 5A.

claim: Tight junction protein 1 (tjp1), also known as zonula occludens-1 (ZO-1), is a scaffolding protein that has two orthologues in zebrafish (tjp1a and tjp1b) (Anderson et al., 1988; Stevenson et al., 1986).
source: We considered that tight junctions may form between HSPCs and ECs and would be marked by tight junction protein 1 (tjp1), the scaffolding protein also known as zonula occludens-1 (ZO-1) that has two orthologues in zebrafish (tjp1a and tjp1b) (Anderson et al., 1988; Stevenson et al., 1986).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Anderson et al., 1988 and Stevenson et al., 1986, representing established knowledge about ZO-1.

claim: ZO-1 was observed broadly on ECs, as well as localized between Runx:mCherry HSPCs and surrounding niche cells.
source: We observed expression of ZO-1 broadly on ECs, as well as localization between Runx:mCherry HSPCs and surrounding niche cells (Figure 2A and B).
evidence: This claim is supported by immunofluorescence data shown in Figure 2A and B.

claim: Tight junctions form at the contact points between HSPCs and the niche.
source: These data suggest that tight junctions form at the contact points between HSPCs and the niche.
evidence: This claim is inferred from the ZO-1 localization data shown in Figure 2A and B.

claim: 57% (n=16/28) of HSPCs were in direct contact with an MSC, 29% were <5 μm (n=8/28), and 14% (n=4/28) were <10 μm away.
source: We measured the distance between HSPCs and MSCs and observed 57% (n=16/28) of HSPCs were in direct contact with an MSC, 29% were <5 μm (n=8/28), and 14% (n=4/28) were <10 μm away (Figure 2D).
evidence: This claim is supported by quantification data shown in Figure 2D.

claim: The data from the larval KM niche are very similar to previous observations from the CHT showing that the majority of HSPCs are in contact with, or close proximity to, an MSC (Tamplin et al., 2015).
source: These data from the larval KM niche are very similar to previous observations from the CHT showing that the majority of HSPCs are in contact with, or close proximity to, an MSC (Tamplin et al., 2015).
evidence: This claim compares current data with previous findings, supported by citation to Tamplin et al., 2015.

claim: HSPC lodgement in the larval KM niche occurs close to or in contact with a single MSC, and HSPCs are in contact with multiple ECs.
source: Together, our results demonstrate that HSPC lodgement in the larval KM niche occurs close to or in contact with a single MSC, and that HSPCs are in contact with multiple ECs, similar to what we observed previously in the CHT.
evidence: This claim summarizes findings from the study, supported by data shown in Figures 1 and 2.

claim: Serial section electron microscopy has been used to resolve the projectome of the complete zebrafish larval brain (Hildebrand et al., 2017).
source: One approach to analyze the ultrastructure of an entire region of tissue is serial section electron microscopy (EM), a technique that has been used to resolve the projectome of the complete zebrafish larval brain (Hildebrand et al., 2017).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to Hildebrand et al., 2017.

claim: CLEM based on anatomical landmarks was previously used to match the position of fluorescently labeled HSPCs in the CHT niche between confocal and SBEM datasets (Tamplin et al., 2015).
source: We previously used CLEM based on anatomical landmarks to match the position of fluorescently labeled HSPCs in the CHT niche between confocal and SBEM datasets (Tamplin et al., 2015).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to Tamplin et al., 2015.

claim: The CLEM approach based on anatomical landmarks was difficult to apply in the KM because the tissue is much larger and denser than the CHT.
source: However, we found this approach was difficult to apply in the KM because the tissue is much larger and denser than the CHT (Cell Image Library [CIL] accession numbers CIL:54845 and CIL:54850).
evidence: This claim is based on the authors' experience and is supported by reference to Cell Image Library datasets.

claim: A transgenic construct was generated that expressed mCherry for light microscopy, and APEX2 as a genetic tag that allowed electron-dense contrast on target subcellular structures.
source: The first step in Workflow #1 was to generate a transgenic construct that expressed mCherry for light microscopy, and APEX2 as a genetic tag that allowed electron-dense contrast on target subcellular structures (Figure 3A).
evidence: This is a methodological claim describing the construct design shown in Figure 3A.

claim: APEX2 was fused with H2B and mito tags for localization to the nucleus and the mitochondrial matrix, respectively.
source: We fused APEX2 with H2B and mito tags for localization to the nucleus and the mitochondrial matrix, respectively.
evidence: This is a methodological claim describing the construct design.

claim: The drl promoter is a marker of vascular and hematopoietic lineages (Herbomel et al., 1999; Mosimann et al., 2015).
source: The drl promoter is a marker of vascular and hematopoietic lineages (Herbomel et al., 1999; Mosimann et al., 2015), and we chose it because of its high HSPC expression level compared to other available promoters, such as Runx1+23 (Tamplin et al., 2015; Nottingham et al., 2007) or cd41 (Ma et al., 2011).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Herbomel et al., 1999 and Mosimann et al., 2015.

claim: It was previously confirmed that drl:GFP+ HSPCs almost completely overlap with Runx:mCherry+ HSPCs from embryo to adult (Henninger et al., 2017; Mosimann et al., 2015).
source: Furthermore, it was previously confirmed that drl:GFP+ HSPCs almost completely overlap with Runx:mCherry+ HSPCs from embryo to adult (Henninger et al., 2017; Mosimann et al., 2015).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Henninger et al., 2017 and Mosimann et al., 2015.

claim: Both cd41:GFP+ and selected F0 drl:APEX2+ larvae had similar numbers of positive HSPCs in the mediolateral clusters of the anterior KM niche.
source: Both cd41:GFP+ and selected F0 drl:APEX2+ larvae had similar numbers of positive HSPCs in the mediolateral clusters of the anterior KM niche (Figure 3—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: This claim is supported by quantification data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1B.

claim: Approximately 15% of HSPCs were both mCherry+;APEX2+ and GFP+ when the drl:APEX2-mCherry construct was injected into cd41:GFP transgenic embryos.
source: We gained further confirmation of HSPC-specific expression in F0 drl:APEX2-mCherry+ larvae by injection of the drl:APEX2-mCherry construct into cd41:GFP transgenic embryos, and observed ~15% of HSPCs were both mCherry+;APEX2+ and GFP+ (data not shown).
evidence: This claim is based on experimental data, though the data is not shown in the manuscript.

claim: Transient expression of the drl:APEX2-mCherry construct in F0 larvae can generate sparse labeling of HSPCs in the KM niche with similar frequency to other stable HSPC-specific reporter lines.
source: These data demonstrate that transient expression of the drl:APEX2-mCherry construct in F0 larvae can generate sparse labeling of HSPCs in the KM niche with similar frequency to other stable HSPC-specific reporter lines.
evidence: This claim is based on inference from the comparison data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1B.

claim: Focal charge compensation effectively eliminates specimen charging in SBEM (Deerinck et al., 2018).
source: Using focal charge compensation (Deerinck et al., 2018) which effectively eliminates specimen charging, we obtained a high-resolution SBEM dataset without the need for excessive post-processing alignment.
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to Deerinck et al., 2018.

claim: Clustered hematopoietic cells were observed around the glomerulus in the same region as seen by light sheet microscopy.
source: We also observed clustered hematopoietic cells around the glomerulus in the same region as seen by light sheet microscopy (compare Figure 1—figure supplement 3 and Figure 4—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This claim is supported by comparison of imaging data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 3 and Figure 4—figure supplement 2.

claim: By performing 3D alignments, a single APEX2+ cell in the SBEM dataset was located that was <5 μm from the corresponding mCherry+ HSPC imaged in the light sheet volume.
source: By performing these 3D alignments, we could locate a single APEX2+ cell in the SBEM dataset that was <5 μm from the corresponding mCherry+ HSPC imaged in the light sheet volume (Figure 4D).
evidence: This claim is supported by CLEM alignment data shown in Figure 4D.

claim: The APEX2+ cell had dark nuclear staining with much higher contrast than any of the surrounding cells, confirming the same APEX2+;mCherry+ HSPC was identified across multiple imaging modalities.
source: Furthermore, the APEX2+ cell had dark nuclear staining with much higher contrast than any of the surrounding cells, confirming we had identified the same APEX2+;mCherry+ HSPC across multiple imaging modalities (Figure 4D).
evidence: This claim is supported by SBEM data shown in Figure 4D.

claim: The lodged APEX2+;mCherry+ HSPC was enclosed in a pocket of five ECs, and attached to a single MSC, that all directly contact the surface of the HSPC.
source: This morphological analysis revealed that the lodged APEX2+;mCherry+ HSPC (Figure 5A) was enclosed in a pocket of five ECs, and attached to a single MSC, that all directly contact the surface of the HSPC (Figure 5B; Figure 5—video 1).
evidence: This claim is supported by 3D modeling data shown in Figure 5A, 5B, and Figure 5—video 1.

claim: The cellular configuration of an HSPC enclosed in a pocket of five ECs and attached to a single MSC was seen previously in the CHT (Tamplin et al., 2015), demonstrating that this cellular structure is also conserved in the larval KM niche.
source: This same configuration of cells was seen previously in the CHT (Tamplin et al., 2015), demonstrating that this cellular structure is also conserved in the larval KM niche.
evidence: This claim compares current findings with previous data, supported by citation to Tamplin et al., 2015.

claim: Ganglion-like cells were identified in the larval KM in direct contact with the APEX2+;mCherry+ HSPC.
source: Careful analysis of our SBEM dataset and the cells in direct contact with the APEX2+;mCherry+ HSPC identified ganglion-like cells in the larval KM (Figure 5B and C; Figure 5—video 1).
evidence: This claim is supported by SBEM data shown in Figure 5B, 5C, and Figure 5—video 1.

claim: The ganglion-like cell was part of a chain of at least eight morphologically similar cells that extended throughout the larval KM niche.
source: The ability to move through all adjacent sections of the 3D SBEM dataset allowed us to follow the length of these ganglion-like cells and discover that it was part of a chain of at least eight morphologically similar cells that extended throughout the larval KM niche.
evidence: This claim is supported by analysis of the 3D SBEM dataset.

claim: Two unlabeled cells with the distinctive morphology of putative HSPCs (HSPC2 and HSPC3) were identified in contact with the APEX2+;mCherry+ HSPC.
source: Further tracing of the neighboring cells in contact with the APEX2+;mCherry+ HSPC revealed two unlabeled cells with the distinctive morphology of putative HSPCs (i.e., scant cytoplasm, large round nucleus, ruffled membrane; HSPC2 and HSPC3; Figure 5B and C).
evidence: This claim is supported by SBEM data shown in Figure 5B and C.

claim: The two unlabeled putative HSPCs were APEX2 negative, suggesting they were not progeny derived by division from the APEX2+;mCherry+ HSPC, and were more likely independent HSPC clones that had lodged in the same niche.
source: These other two putative HSPCs were APEX2 negative, suggesting they were not progeny derived by division from the APEX2+;mCherry+ HSPC, and were more likely independent HSPC clones that had lodged in the same niche.
evidence: This claim is based on inference from the APEX2 negative status of the cells.

claim: All three HSPCs were in direct contact with the chain of ganglion-like cells that extends through the larval KM niche.
source: All three HSPCs were in direct contact with the chain of ganglion-like cells that we found extends through the larval KM niche (Figure 5C; Figure 5—video 1).
evidence: This claim is supported by 3D modeling data shown in Figure 5C and Figure 5—video 1.

claim: A single endogenous HSPC can be in direct physical contact with as many as eight other cells.
source: This 3D SBEM dataset allowed identification of all surrounding cells in contact with the APEX2+;mCherry+ HSPC, and strikingly showed that a single endogenous HSPC can be in direct physical contact with as many as eight other cells.
evidence: This claim is based on counting all cells in contact with the APEX2+;mCherry+ HSPC in the SBEM dataset.

claim: Two unlabeled putative HSPCs were found in the perivascular regions of a second SBEM dataset, each in its own pocket of five ECs and attached to a single MSC.
source: We searched the perivascular regions of the larval KM niche within this second SBEM dataset and found two unlabeled putative HSPCs. Not only did both putative HSPCs share a distinct morphology, but following 3D modeling of all surrounding niche cells in contact with the HSPCs, we found each one was also in its own pocket of five ECs, and attached to a single MSC, exactly as we had observed previously in the CHT (Tamplin et al., 2015), and with the APEX2+;mCherry+ labeled HSPC (compare Figure 5C and Figure 5—figure supplement 3).
evidence: This claim is supported by SBEM data shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 3 and comparison with Figure 5C.

claim: One of the unlabeled putative HSPCs was also in contact with a chain of ganglion-like cells.
source: Furthermore, one of the unlabeled putative HSPCs was also in contact with a chain of ganglion-like cells (Figure 5—figure supplement 3).
evidence: This claim is supported by SBEM data shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 3.

claim: Using just the anatomical location and distinctive morphology of an HSPC, the 3D niche configuration of two more putative HSPCs in the larval KM niche could be reconstructed.
source: In summary, using just the anatomical location and distinctive morphology of an HSPC, we could reconstruct the 3D niche configuration of two more putative HSPCs in the larval KM niche.
evidence: This claim summarizes the findings from the second SBEM dataset analysis.

claim: The software predicted 10 cd41:GFP+ HSPCs in the confocal Z stack, and all of those cells overlapped with traced models of the nearest putative HSPC in the SBEM dataset.
source: The software predicted 10 cd41:GFP+ HSPCs in the confocal Z stack, and all of those cells overlapped with traced models of the nearest putative HSPC in the SBEM dataset (Figure 6—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This claim is supported by software analysis and manual tracing data shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 1.

claim: Extensive tracing of putative HSPCs in the SBEM dataset revealed an additional seven cells that were not well defined by their GFP signal in the confocal dataset.
source: Interestingly, extensive tracing of putative HSPCs in the SBEM dataset revealed an additional seven cells that were not well defined by their GFP signal in the confocal dataset (Figure 6—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This claim is supported by manual tracing data shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 2.

claim: The additional seven putative HSPCs were all deeper in the sample, so were either GFP- or not detected because of low GFP signal.
source: These putative HSPCs were all deeper in the sample, so were either GFP- or not detected because of low GFP signal.
evidence: This claim is based on inference from the position of the cells in the sample and their GFP signal.

claim: Regardless of their location, all putative HSPCs were in contact with between 2 and 6 ECs.
source: Regardless of their location, all putative HSPCs were in contact with between 2 and 6 ECs.
evidence: This claim is based on analysis of all putative HSPCs in the SBEM datasets, summarized in Table 1.

claim: 50% of putative HSPCs were in contact with a single MSC (n=11/22).
source: Strikingly, 50% of putative HSPCs were in contact with a single MSC (n=11/22; Table 1), similar to what we found by light microscopy in the larval KM niche (60% cd41:GFP+ HSPCs in contact with cxcl12:DsRed2+ MSC; Figure 2), and previously in the CHT (60% Runx:GFP+ HSPCs in contact with cxcl12:DsRed2+ MSC; Tamplin et al., 2015).
evidence: This claim is supported by quantification data summarized in Table 1 and comparison with data in Figure 2 and citation to Tamplin et al., 2015.

claim: Considerable heterogeneity exists between the different structural configurations of a single HSPC and its surrounding niche cells.
source: Considering all our SBEM data together (Table 1), we have also identified considerable heterogeneity between the different structural configurations of a single HSPC and its surrounding niche cells.
evidence: This claim is based on analysis of all SBEM data summarized in Table 1.

claim: The structural heterogeneity between sites of HSPC lodgement suggests that there could be functional heterogeneity as well between different sites of hematopoiesis in the microenvironment.
source: This suggests that there could be functional heterogeneity as well between different sites of hematopoiesis in the microenvironment.
evidence: This claim is speculative, based on inference from the observed structural heterogeneity.

claim: dbh+ sympathetic ganglion cells are found in the larval KM region at 5 dpf (An et al., 2002; Stewart et al., 2006; Stewart et al., 2004; Zhu et al., 2012).
source: In the zebrafish larva, dbh+ sympathetic ganglion cells are found in the larval KM region at 5 dpf (An et al., 2002; Stewart et al., 2006; Stewart et al., 2004; Zhu et al., 2012).
evidence: This claim is supported by multiple citations documenting the presence of dbh+ cells in the larval KM.

claim: dbh:GFP+ cell projections were observed in contact with or in close proximity to mCherry+ HSPCs.
source: We crossed the dbh:GFP (Zhu et al., 2012) and Runx:mCherry transgenic lines, and observed dbh:GFP+ cell projections in contact with or in close proximity to mCherry+ HSPCs (Figure 7A and B; Figure 7—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: This claim is supported by imaging data shown in Figure 7A, 7B, and Figure 7—figure supplement 1A.

claim: Chemical inhibition of dbh during KM colonization significantly reduced the number of lodged HSPCs.
source: Chemical inhibition of dbh during KM colonization significantly reduced the number of lodged HSPCs.
evidence: This claim is based on the 6-OHDA treatment experiment, with data shown in Figure 7C.

claim: A significant reduction in the number of Runx:mCherry+ HSPCs within the niche was observed after treatment with 6-OHDA.
source: We observed a significant reduction in the number of Runx:mCherry+ HSPCs within the niche after treatment with this dopaminergic cell neurotoxin (Figure 7C; Figure 7—figure supplement 1C, D).
evidence: This claim is supported by quantification data shown in Figure 7C and Figure 7—figure supplement 1C, D.

claim: dbh:GFP+ cells aligned with ganglion-like cells in the KM niche.
source: dbh:GFP+ cells aligned with ganglion-like cells in the KM niche.
evidence: This claim is based on CLEM alignment of dbh:GFP+ cells with SBEM data.

claim: One ganglion-like cell was identified in contact with a lodged cell that morphologically resembled an HSPC.
source: We identified one ganglion-like cell in contact with a lodged cell that morphologically resembled an HSPC, with the caveat that this cell lacks an independent marker of HSPC identity (Figure 7D; Figure 7—figure supplement 1B; Figure 7—videos 1; 2).
evidence: This claim is supported by SBEM data shown in Figure 7D, Figure 7—figure supplement 1B, and Figure 7—videos 1 and 2.

claim: dbh+ ganglion-like cells are present in the larval KM niche and are in direct contact with putative HSPCs.
source: We have confirmed that dbh+ ganglion-like cells are present in the larval KM niche and are in direct contact with putative HSPCs.
evidence: This claim summarizes findings from the dbh:GFP CLEM experiments and functional studies.

claim: Previous studies have shown that dopamine signaling regulates HSPC function in the mammalian bone marrow (Afan et al., 1997; Katayama et al., 2006; Liu et al., 2021; Méndez-Ferrer et al., 2008).
source: Previous studies have shown that dopamine signaling regulates HSPC function in the mammalian bone marrow (Afan et al., 1997; Katayama et al., 2006; Liu et al., 2021; Méndez-Ferrer et al., 2008).
evidence: This claim is supported by multiple citations documenting the role of dopamine signaling in HSPC regulation.

claim: A previous study indicated that disrupting dopamine signaling during early stages of development (five somite stage to 30 hpf) resulted in reduced HSPC numbers within the CHT at 48 hpf (Kwan et al., 2016).
source: A previous study indicated that disrupting dopamine signaling during early stages of development (five somite stage to 30 hours post fertilization (hpf)) resulted in reduced HSPC numbers within the CHT at 48 hpf (Kwan et al., 2016).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to Kwan et al., 2016.

claim: The findings are consistent with the established role for neuronal regulation of HSPCs in zebrafish and mammals (Agarwala and Tamplin, 2018).
source: Our findings are consistent with the established role for neuronal regulation of HSPCs in zebrafish and mammals (Agarwala and Tamplin, 2018).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to Agarwala and Tamplin, 2018.

claim: dbh+ cells originate from the same neural crest lineage as a subtype of fetal bone marrow MSCs (An et al., 2002; Isern et al., 2014).
source: Intriguingly, these dbh+ cells originate from the same neural crest lineage as a subtype of fetal bone marrow MSCs (An et al., 2002; Isern et al., 2014).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to An et al., 2002 and Isern et al., 2014.

claim: CLEM is a viable approach to identify single rare stem cells deep in live tissue.
source: Together, our results have demonstrated that CLEM is a viable approach to identify single rare stem cells deep in live tissue, and that 3D models of a stem cell in its niche built from SBEM data provides a complete picture of stem cell-niche interactions.
evidence: This claim summarizes the overall conclusion of the study based on the experimental results.

claim: 3D models of a stem cell in its niche built from SBEM data provide a complete picture of stem cell-niche interactions.
source: Together, our results have demonstrated that CLEM is a viable approach to identify single rare stem cells deep in live tissue, and that 3D models of a stem cell in its niche built from SBEM data provides a complete picture of stem cell-niche interactions.
evidence: This claim summarizes the overall conclusion of the study based on the experimental results.

claim: Drosophila equivalent occludin junctions have been found to regulate niche interactions with hematopoietic cells and germline stem cells (Fairchild et al., 2016; Khadilkar et al., 2017).
source: Interestingly, Drosophila equivalent occludin junctions have been found to regulate niche interactions with hematopoietic cells and germline stem cells (Fairchild et al., 2016; Khadilkar et al., 2017).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Fairchild et al., 2016 and Khadilkar et al., 2017.

claim: Recent studies showed that subtypes of ECs within the vasculature of the mouse bone marrow microenvironment provide different regulatory functions (Zhang et al., 2021).
source: Recent studies showed that subtypes of ECs within the vasculature of the mouse bone marrow microenvironment provide different regulatory functions (Zhang et al., 2021).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to Zhang et al., 2021.

claim: The heterogeneity between sites of HSPC lodgement and their surrounding niche cells supports the model that functionally distinct sites exist within the hematopoietic microenvironment (Zhang et al., 2021).
source: The heterogeneity between sites of HSPC lodgement and their surrounding niche cells supports the model that functionally distinct sites exist within the hematopoietic microenvironment (Zhang et al., 2021).
evidence: This claim is based on inference from the observed heterogeneity and is supported by citation to Zhang et al., 2021.

claim: The zebrafish larva is transparent, allowing visualization of internal tissues.
source: We have taken advantage of the transparency and external development of the zebrafish larva to study the earliest migration events of HSPCs into the presumptive adult kidney marrow (KM) niche.
evidence: This is established knowledge about zebrafish larvae that is implicit in the choice of model organism.

claim: The zebrafish larva develops externally.
source: We have taken advantage of the transparency and external development of the zebrafish larva to study the earliest migration events of HSPCs into the presumptive adult kidney marrow (KM) niche.
evidence: This is established knowledge about zebrafish larvae that is implicit in the choice of model organism.

claim: The larval KM at 5 dpf represents the earliest stages of HSPC colonization of the presumptive adult kidney marrow niche.
source: We have taken advantage of the transparency and external development of the zebrafish larva to study the earliest migration events of HSPCs into the presumptive adult kidney marrow (KM) niche.
evidence: This is inferred from the study design focusing on 4-5 dpf larvae.

claim: The cd41:GFP transgenic line labels HSPCs.
source: We also examined expression of the cd41:GFP HSPC reporter line in the region of the anterior KM and found substantial overlap with Runx:mCherry+ HSPCs (Figure 1—figure supplement 5A).
evidence: This is established knowledge about the cd41:GFP reporter line, confirmed by overlap with Runx:mCherry+ HSPCs.

claim: The flk:ZsGreen transgenic line labels endothelial cells.
source: To determine the location of these HSPC clusters relative to the vasculature, we imaged HSPC-specific Runx:mCherry together with the flk:ZsGreen vascular-specific transgenic reporter (Cross et al., 2003).
evidence: This is established knowledge about the flk:ZsGreen reporter line, supported by citation to Cross et al., 2003.

claim: The cdh17:GFP transgenic line labels pronephric tubules.
source: Together with the cdh17:GFP reporter line for pronephric tubules (Zhou et al., 2010), we localized Runx:mCherry+ HSPCs within the anterior kidney region, mediolateral to the proximal pronephric tubules (Figure 1—figure supplement 3).
evidence: This is established knowledge about the cdh17:GFP reporter line, supported by citation to Zhou et al., 2010.

claim: The cxcl12:DsRed2 transgenic line labels mesenchymal stromal cells.
source: We then went on to characterize additional niche cell types that are present in the larval KM. We performed imaging using the cd41:GFP HSPC transgenic reporter line together with cxcl12:DsRed2 (Glass et al., 2011) to label MSCs (Figure 2C).
evidence: This is established knowledge about the cxcl12:DsRed2 reporter line, supported by citation to Glass et al., 2011.

claim: Alpha-bungarotoxin can be used to paralyze zebrafish larvae.
source: At 5 dpf, larvae with circulating mCherry+ HSPCs were injected retro-orbitally with alpha-bungarotoxin and dextran-conjugated Oregon Green dye, to paralyze the larvae and label the vasculature, respectively (Figure 3C).
evidence: This is established knowledge about the use of alpha-bungarotoxin, supported by citation to Swinburne et al., 2015 in the Methods section.

claim: Oregon Green dextran can be used to label the vasculature in zebrafish larvae.
source: At 5 dpf, larvae with circulating mCherry+ HSPCs were injected retro-orbitally with alpha-bungarotoxin and dextran-conjugated Oregon Green dye, to paralyze the larvae and label the vasculature, respectively (Figure 3C).
evidence: This is established knowledge about the use of fluorescent dextrans to label vasculature.

claim: DAB staining can be used to label APEX2+ cells for identification by brightfield microscopy.
source: Larvae were stained with DAB to label APEX2+ cells for identification by brightfield microscopy (Figure 3E).
evidence: This is established knowledge about APEX2-DAB staining, supported by citations to Lam et al., 2015 and related methods.

claim: MicroCT can be used to orient and trim embedded samples for SBEM.
source: Larvae were treated with osmium tetroxide and embedded for micro-computed tomography (microCT; Figure 3F and Figure 3—figure supplement 2; Figure 3—video 2). This intermediate microCT step allowed the larvae to be oriented and trimmed to select a discrete region of interest (ROI) for SBEM (Figure 3G and Figure 3—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This is a methodological approach described in the study.

claim: DRAQ5 is a nuclear DNA binding fluorescent dye.
source: Briefly, GFP+ transgenic larvae were fixed, sectioned using a vibratome, incubated with DRAQ5 fluorescent nuclear dye, and imaged by confocal microscopy.
evidence: This is established knowledge about DRAQ5, which is a commercially available nuclear dye.

claim: Illumination of DRAQ5 can trigger DAB polymerization through generation of reactive oxygen species.
source: After imaging, DAB staining solution was added to the sections, followed by illumination to photooxidize DRAQ5. This step locally generates reactive oxygen species that trigger DAB polymerization and darkening of the nuclei (Ou et al., 2017).
evidence: This is established knowledge about DRAQ5 photooxidation, supported by citation to Ou et al., 2017.

claim: 6-OHDA is a neurotoxin that induces lesions in dopaminergic neurons.
source: To understand the functional significance of dopamine signaling during KM niche colonization, we treated Runx:mCherry+ larvae with 6-hydroxydopamine (6-OHDA), a neurotoxin that induces lesions in dopaminergic neurons (Jackson-Lewis et al., 2012; Matsui and Sugie, 2017; Vijayanathan et al., 2017).
evidence: This is established knowledge about 6-OHDA, supported by multiple citations.

claim: 6-OHDA treatment reduces locomotor activity in zebrafish larvae.
source: We confirmed the efficacy of the drug treatment by reduced locomotor activity (Feng et al., 2014) of the larvae (data not shown).
evidence: This is established knowledge about the effects of 6-OHDA, supported by citation to Feng et al., 2014.
